scenario.name: MITRE ATLAS AML.T0010, Trail of Bits fickling & HuggingFace Security — PyTorch Pickle Model Checkpoint Deserialization Forensics
scenario.shortSubtitle: AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security · T1195.002
scenario.overview: Imagine a research lab downloading a shared suitcase of pre-trained brain weights from a public model exchange. Tucked inside the suitcase lining is a hidden wind-up instruction card that springs open the very instant an engineer unzips the suitcase using an older loading table without a safety tray, launching covert workshop commands before the model weights are even examined. In this scenario (T1195.002, MITRE ATLAS AML.T0010, Trail of Bits fickling & HuggingFace Security, PyTorch Pickle Model Checkpoint Deserialization Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: pyTorch ZIP Archive Inspection, then legacy torch.load Invocation Without, then runtime eBPF / Sysmon Detection of Python. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering PyTorch ZIP Archive Inspection, then Legacy torch.load Invocation Without, then Runtime eBPF / Sysmon Detection of Python, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1195.002 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: PyTorch ZIP Archive Inspection & Pickle Opcode Disassembly (pickletools / fickling)
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: ML Model Checkpoint / AML.T0010)
stages.description: Before putting the downloaded suitcase onto the lab bench, a cautious inspector opens the outer zipper and reads the packing manifest line by line, discovering wind-up command gears hidden right beside the harmless numeric weight pouches. Standard PyTorch .pt and .bin checkpoints are ZIP archives containing tensor storage files alongside archive/data.pkl. Disassembling data.pkl with python3 -m pickletools or fickling reveals STACK_GLOBAL / REDUCE opcodes referencing posix.system, subprocess.Popen, or builtins.eval (logged in Linux Audit Event 10 with ModelArchive=model_weights.pt , archive/data.pkl, DangerousOpcodes=STACK_GLOBAL , 'posix', 'system' + REDUCE , 0x52, AtlasTechnique=MITRE ATLAS AML.T0010 , ML Supply Chain Compromise so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes python3 -m pickletools -a archive/data.pkl | grep -E "GLOBAL|STACK_GLOBAL|REDUCE" (which inspects or executes AI/ML infrastructure operations , python3 -m pickletools -a archive/data.pkl | grep -E "GLOBAL|STACK_GLOBAL|REDUCE" across Ray so that exposes unauthenticated ML cluster job submission, unsafe model checkpoint deserialization, or indirect prompt injection via RAG context retrieval , T1195.002 during "PyTorch ZIP Archive Inspection & Pickle Opcode Disassembly , pickletools / fickling"). Next, the follow-up artifact fickling --check-safety -p model_weights.pt runs (which inspects or executes AI/ML infrastructure operations , fickling --check-safety -p model_weights.pt across Ray Dashboard Jobs API , :8265/api/jobs/ so that exposes unauthenticated ML cluster job submission, unsafe model checkpoint deserialization, or indirect prompt injection via RAG context retrieval , T1195.002 during "PyTorch ZIP Archive Inspection & Pickle Opcode Disassembly , pickletools / fickling"). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ fickling --check-safety -p model_weights.pt / ⇠#1 ACK 10) from Node ① (#1 Model Hub Repository (.pt/.bin)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Safetensors / weights_only Gate).

stages.title: Stage 2: Legacy torch.load() Invocation Without weights_only=True Triggering __reduce__()
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1203 - Deserialization of Untrusted Data in torch.load)
stages.description: On an unprotected training bench, the engineer places the suitcase onto the legacy automatic unpacker without flipping the weights-only safety lock, causing the hidden wind-up card to snap open and execute its command before the model weights even reach the table. When an inference or fine-tuning script calls torch.load("model_weights.pt") without weights_only=True, Python pickle.Unpickler executes the REDUCE opcode immediately during deserialization, before the model state_dict is even returned to the caller (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with ParentInferenceProcess=python3 inference_server.py , PID 8810, UnpicklerHook=pickle._Unpickler.load_reduce, -> posix.system, MitigationCheck=torch.load..., weights_only=True so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes python3 -c "import torch; torch.load('model_weights.pt', weights_only=True)" (which inspects or executes AI/ML infrastructure operations , python3 -c "import torch; torch.load, 'model_weights.pt', weights_only=True" across Ray Dash so that exposes unauthenticated ML cluster job submission, unsafe model checkpoint deserialization, or indirect prompt injection via RAG context retrieval , T1203 during "Legacy torch.load, Invocation Without weights_only=True Triggering __reduce__,"). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ python3 inference_server.py --checkpoint model_weights.pt / ⇠#2 ACK 59) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 archive/data.pkl Pickle Stream), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Safetensors / weights_only Gate).

keySpecs.value: Always pass weights_only=True to torch.load() (the default in PyTorch 2.6+), which restricts the unpickler to primitive tensor reconstruction types only.

stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1027 - Obfuscated Pickle Bytecode / Runtime Behavioral Catch)
stages.description: Even when the saboteur disguises the wind-up card using clever mirror chains to fool front-desk X-ray scanners, the lab’s runtime motion alarm fires the instant the quiet math-inference worker unexpectedly reaches for a power drill or dials an outside telephone line. Even if a malicious pickle payload uses obfuscated builtins.getattr chains to bypass static pickle scanners, runtime monitoring catches the Python inference worker process invoking sys_execve or initiating outbound connections to untrusted IPs (logged in Linux Audit Event 42 with RuntimeRule=Falco: Python AI Inference Process Spawned Shell, ParentProcess=python3 , Model Loader, RecommendedFormat=HuggingFace .safetensors so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -k python_pickle_exec -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -k python_pickle_exec -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exac so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1027 during "Runtime eBPF / Sysmon Detection of Python Inference Worker Spawning Subprocesses" , Even if a malicious pickle payload uses obfuscated builtins while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -F ppid=8810 -k python_pickle_exec / ⇠#3 ACK 42) from Node ③ (#3 archive/data.pkl Pickle Stream) to Node ④ (#4 Python torch.load() Process), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Safetensors / weights_only Gate).
